projects.name: IFAD - 2000002987 (UNDP)– Amazon Sustainable Management achieved (Amazon Sustainable Management Project PAGES)
projects.description:
PAGES’ goal is to contribute to reducing rural poverty while decreasing deforestation and environmental degradation in the Amazon region of Maranhão. Its development objective is to improve the livelihoods and the food and nutrition security of the rural poor through the conservation and sustainable use of the Amazon rainforest. Through the intervention, the project will increase the resilience of 64,000 people and reduce approximately 6 million tons of CO2 equivalent. The intervention area comprises three development regions in the state: Maranhense Amazon, Maranhense Gurupi, and Pindaré. The target group includes 20,000 organized family farms facing poverty and associated with rural organizations (approximately 80,000 people), at least 12,5% of which are from 2,500 indigenous and other traditional communities (about 1,200 indigenous families, 800 quilombolas, and 500 coconut breakers), 50% women and 25% young people.

Actual start date: 15/05/2022
Actual end date: 30/06/2028

Financial Information:
Total cost: US$ 37 million
IFAD Donation: US$ 17 million (ASAP+ through German Gov.)
State Government counterpart: US$ 16 million
Beneficiary contribution: US$ 4 million

projects.description:
Project: TAPAJÓS: A Prevalence-based Project to Reduce Forced Labor (Tapajós).
Actual start date: 01/10/2021.

This project aims to reduce the prevalence of forced labour in the gold mining sector in the State of Pará following evidence-based interventions to prevent trafficking in persons (TiP) and forced labour, protect victims and prosecute traffickers/explorers. Tapajós's Phase I was focused on producing knowledge on (a) the prevalence of TiP and forced labour, (b) the production chain of gold mining in the region, and (c) the convergence of crimes. The project's Phase II now targets applying evidence-based intervention to reach its goal. It is implemented under the United Nations Convention against Transnational Organized Crime's Protocol to Prevent, Suppress and Punish Trafficking in Persons, especially Women and Children and the Protocol against the Smuggling of Migrants by Land, Sea and Air.

projects.name: UNEP Promoting integrated metropolitan planning and innovative urban technology investments in Brazil - CITinova II
projects.description:
The main challenge addressed by this project is that Brazilian metropolitan areas are growing unsustainably, based on an inefficient development model characterized by a high degree of urban sprawl, which has several negative consequences for the environment, including high levels of GHG emissions, significant loss of biodiversity, habitat fragmentation and increased pressures on ecosystem services. This model also makes urban governance costly and complex, and ultimately degrades quality of life in urban areas.
To address the aforementioned global environmental problems that Brazil is experiencing in an urban context, this project aims to accelerate the sustainable development of Brazilian metropolitan regions, Leading lo reductions in greenhouse gas emissions and the conservation of biodiversity. To this end, the project will increase local, state and federal capacity to undertake integrated urban planning, catalyze sustainable investments and facilitate long-term and sustainable urban development. Ultimately, the project aims to contribute toa sustainable transformation of the country's urban system and its development pattern.
To ensure the achievement of its objective, this project will focus on three distinct but representative metropolitan regions in Brazil, in addition to focusing on replicating and scaling-up good practices at the national level. The three pilot metropolitan regions are:
(1) Belém Metropolitan Region (RM Belém), located in the State of Pará in the northem and Amazonian region of the country;
(2) Greater Teresina Integrated Developmeot Region (Greater Teresina RIDE), in the northeast region in the states of Piauí and Maranhão. For most activities, the project will focus on the RIDE's ptimary urban area, the Timon-Teresina Urban Agglomeration; and,
(3) Florianópolis Metropolitan Region (RM Florianópolis), located in the State of Santa Catarina, in the southern region of the country.

projects.name: UNEP IRI Phase 2: “Interfaith Rainforest Initiative 2021-2024 – Expansion of faith-based movements for forests, climate change and the rights of Indigenous Peoples and local communities”
projects.description:
The Interfaith Rainforest Initiative (IRI) is an international alliance that is bringing moral urgency and faith-based leadership to global efforts to halt and reverse tropical deforestation. 

IRI began actual implementation during a Phase 1 that took place from September 2018 to August 2021. IRI Phase 1 (SMA ID: 38843; PS Project ID: SB-011041; Project Title: “Interfaith Rainforest Initiative”) was also implemented by UNEP with financial support from NICFI. IRI Phase 1 aimed at establishing platforms both globally and at the country level in key rainforest countries to catalyze the influence, advocacy, and moral commitment of religious leaders and faith-based communities for the protection of tropical rainforests. 

In Phase 2, the Initiative deepened and expanded its body of work upon the results achieved in Phase 1. The project vision was developed based on lessons learned from Phase 1, a series of strategy and planning meetings held with the Initiative’s Global Steering Committee, participatory discussions, consultations with the IRI country counterparts, and informed by the findings of an external assessment coordinated by the Government of Norway. IRI Phase 2 included a comprehensive body of work aiming to contribute to longer term impacts.

projects.name: UNEP Implementation of the Strategic Action Programme to ensure Integrated and Sustainable Management of the Transboundary Water Resources of the Amazon River Basin Considering Climate Variability and Change
projects.description:
The Project's overarching goal is to aid basin countries in implementing the Strategic Action Programme (SAP), fostering Integrated Water Resources Management (IWRM) in a source-to-sea continuum. This approach aims to deliver ecological, social, and economic benefits, supporting Amazon riparian countries in meeting sustainable development goals (SDGs) and convention targets. The Project operates through four key Components:
The Project is being executed through four Components:
Component 1 will strengthen the current national and regional institutional IWRM framework and develop a financial sustainability strategy to facilitate fund raising for SAP implementation, as well as ACTO’s role in conservation finance for improved IWRM. 
Components 2 will build community resilience to address the impacts of climate change in the Amazon Basin in order to reduce damages from extreme climactic events; ensure water security in the context of adaptation to climate change; and enhance resilience of coastal ecosystems. The component will also touch on the issues of infrastructure resilience in the context of climate change, promoting technical dialogue on infrastructure resilience and sustainability, facilitating exchange of best practices on risk analysis and environmental impact assessment and improving understanding of the Nexus and progress towards achievement of SDG9 in the Amazon basin. 
Component 3 will implement integrated environmental and water resources monitoring systems in order to establish basin wide compatible information to guide science-to-policy decision-making in IWRM and for conservation and protection of the bio-aquatic ecosystems. A supplement to the existing TDA/SAP and National Action Plans (NAP) using TWAP indicators will facilitate interconnections between national and regional activities, supporting national reports related to international conventions and SDGs. 
Component 4 provides project management tools, as well as a system to monitor SAP implementation over time. This component will also promote project visibility within the Amazon Basin and worldwide, facilitating ACTO’s positioning and recognition as an IWRM coordination agency for the Amazon Basin.
The Amazon Cooperation Treaty Organization (ACTO) is the Executing Agency for the Project. National government partners include: Ministries of Foreign Affairs in the 8 basin countries, Ministry of Environment and Water (Bolivia), National Water and Basic Sanitation Agency (Brazil), Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development (Colombia), Ministry of Environment, Water and Ecological Transition (Ecuador), Ministry of Agriculture / Hydromet Service (Guyana), National Water Authority (Peru), Ministry of Spatial Planning and Environment (Suriname), and the People’s Power Ministry for Eco-socialism and the PP Ministry of Atention to Water (Venezuela).

#SSC Colombia, Ecuador, Guyana, Peru, Suriname.
Project: Combating Transnational Conservation Crimes in the Amazon (ECOS).
Actual start date: 01/03/2021.

This project aims to improve regional cooperation and capacity of enforcement and justice system actors to detect, interdict, investigate and prosecute transnational conservation crimes (TCCs) in the Amazon. To reach that, it focuses on (a) improving information exchange and regional cooperation between the Amazon countries, and (b) enhancing the capacity of enforcement and justice system actors to respond to TCCs. It acts on four main axis: forest crimes, wildlife trafficking, illegal fishing, and minerals-related crimes. It is implemented under the United Nations Convention against Transnational Organized Crime and in line with the Global Programme on Crimes that Affect the Environment.

CWDR enables conditions for WHRDs to strengthen solidarity, skills, and communication among WHRDs for early warning and self-protection against threats and violence. Project                      : BRA/21/01/USA (108234)  - Decent work through Skills and Livelihoods training for groups vulnerable to discrimination							
Agreement Dates     : 08-JUL-2021 - 15-JUN-2025

This project addresses three key issues:

- Ensuring that a successful approach to employment training for groups vulnerable to discrimination on grounds sensitive to gender and covered by international labour and human rights standards is adapted and more widely available both in terms of potential trainees and in occupations covered.

- Building the capacity of government, employers’, workers’ and civil society organizations to realize objectives of national strategies on decent work for these groups; and

- Disseminating models, methodologies, strategies and the lessons learned and for replication in states in Brazil.

The project builds on the success and achievements of a programme of employment training and workforce engagement for persons in vulnerability, adapting the learning to address the unique needs of specific groups seeking decent employment and self-employment.

To achieve this objective, the initiative is built on three axis. The first targets companies, institutions and governments on issues and actions related to decent work, social protection and entrepreneurship. The second directly addresses refugee and migrant women, so that they have access to training and opportunities to participate in decision-making processes related to the labor market and entrepreneurship. And the third also targets refugee and migrant women, so that they have knowledge and access to services that respond to gender-based violence.

projects.name: UNODC GLOZ83 CRIMJUST National actors' capacities strengthened to promote transnational investigations, criminal justice actions & cooperation, with a view of disrupting organised crime networks
projects.description:
#SSC Latin America and West Africa.
Project: Criminal Network Disruption Global Programme (CRIMJUST).

CRIMJUST aims contribute to the reduction of the impact of organised crime and related corruption on the security and rule of law of countries along illicit trafficking routes. In January 2023, a new third phase of CRIMJUST was launched to strengthen transnational investigations, criminal justice actions and criminal justice cooperation along illicit trafficking routes in Africa, Latin America, and the Caribbean. This phase focuses on identifying and disrupting organised crime groups and high-level criminal targets, via a three-tier intervention: (a) investigating and prosecuting transnational illicit trafficking, (b) depriving organized crime groups of illicit proceeds, and (c) fostering institutional integrity and promoting Human Rights Standards. CRIMJUST is implemented under UNODC's mandate of the United Nations Convention against Transnational Organized Crime and the Three International Drug Control Conventions.

projects.description: A iniciativa foi um dos resultados adotados pelo gabinete do Secretário-Geral. Para atingir esse objetivo, os parceiros trabalharão para aumentar as ambições em eficiência energética dentro dos NDCs, ajudando na preparação de planos de ação, combinando os governos com os fornecedores de soluções certos. Como organizadora da iniciativa, a UNIDO trabalhará com parceiros na criação de uma equipe de coordenação que ajudará a: (a) envolver novos países para assumirem compromissos mais ambiciosos em matéria de eficiência energética, (b) apoiar os países membros na identificação de prioridades, aumentando a sua sensibilização para as oportunidades de eficiência energética em vários usos finais sectores e desenvolver planos de ação e (c) desenvolver ferramentas harmonizadas para identificação de oportunidades de eficiência energética em vários sectores e garantir a coordenação com vários membros e acompanhar o progresso da iniciativa.

projects.name: UNIDO 210120 Energy, water, food and climate nexus through organic waste to energy solutions in the Metropolitan Region of Recife
projects.description: O projeto pretende lançar as bases para um projeto maior a ser implementado em parceria com o Governo, o sector privado e com o apoio do financiamento climático internacional. O projeto aborda o nexo sensível entre energia, água, alimentos e clima na Região Metropolitana do Recife (RMR), promovendo o uso de resíduos orgânicos em soluções energéticas (WTE). O projeto tem caráter intersetorial e contribui para a implementação de diversas políticas e regulamentações federais, estaduais e urbanas, como o Plano de Resíduos Sólidos da RMR, o Plano Estadual de Resíduos Sólidos de Pernambuco, o Plano de Saneamento do Recife, o Contribuição Nacionalmente Determinada (NDC), bem como o Plano Nacional de Energia para 2050, recentemente adotado, com as suas ambiciosas metas em matéria de energias renováveis. A gestão de resíduos sólidos, água e saneamento, segurança energética e adaptação às mudanças climáticas são as principais preocupações inter-relacionadas da Região Metropolitana de Pernambuco (RMR), que inclui 15 municípios, fornece meios de subsistência para cerca de 4 milhões de pessoas e abriga importantes indústrias da região. O objetivo geral do projeto é abordar o nexo energia, água, alimentos e clima, promovendo o uso de soluções de resíduos orgânicos em energia (WTE) na Região Metropolitana de Pernambuco (RMR).

projects.description: The Accelerate-to-Demonstrate (A2D) Facility aims to accelerate the commercialization of innovative clean energy technologies in developing countries. projects.name: UN WOMEN Multistakeholder partnerships for a transformative change towards gender equality and women’s empowerment expanded (HeforShe, Unstereotype Alliance and WEPs)
projects.description:
Multistakeholders partnerships for a transformative change towards gender equality and women’s empowerment are established by UN Women Brazil to address stereotypes in marketing and communications (Unstereotype Alliance); to engage men as allies (HeForShe); to ensure the workplace is an enabling environment for women (WEPs). The key objective is to ensure that the private sector recognizes the importance and benefits of gender equality, and actively promotes it within and beyond their circles of influence, resulting in cultural and social change at organizational, community and institutional levels, influencing the public agenda. Mobilizing the private sector, not only as a funding source, but as strategic partners for the promotion of decent work for women, providing concrete measures and targets for reaching gender equality in the workplace.   

The Unstereotype Alliance, a thought and action platform that uses advertising as a force for good to drive positive change. It seeks to eradicate harmful gender-based stereotypes. The alliance is focused on empowering women in all their diversity (race, class, age, ability, ethnicity, religion, sexuality, language, education, etc.) and addressing harmful masculinities to help create a gender equal world. The Alliance brings together a powerful growing global coalition of leading industry players behind the common goal of eliminating gender bias and harmful gender stereotypes from their advertising.

The HeForShe solidarity movement for gender equality, which provides a systematic approach and targeted platform on which men and boys can engage and become change agents towards the achievement of gender equality. Achieving gender equality in our lifetimes requires an innovative, inclusive approach that both recognizes men and boys as partners for women’s rights and acknowledges the ways in which they also benefit from this equality. HeForShe invites men and boys to build on the work of the women’s movement as equal partners, crafting and implementing a shared vision of gender equality that will benefit all of humanity.
The Women’s Empowerment Principles (WEPs) are a set of Principles to which companies and organization commit and which offer guidance to business on how to promote gender equality and women’s empowerment in the workplace, marketplace and community. Established by UN Global Compact and UN Women, the WEPs are informed by international labour and human rights standards and grounded in the recognition that businesses have a stake in, and a responsibility for, gender equality and women’s empowerment.

projects.name: UNEP Realizing the Biodiversity Conservation Potential of Private Lands
projects.description:
Half of the remaining natural vegetation cover in the five Brazilian biomes this project focuses on (Atlantic Forest, Cerrado, Caatinga, Pantanal and Pampa), amounting to 88 million hectares of natural vegetation, are located on private lands. Although a massive investment is underway to georeference these areas, with almost 70% national coverage completed, their ability to contribute to biodiversity conservation and ecosystem services provision, which is underpinned by their sustainable landscape and forest management is hindered by a lack of i) management guidelines for landscape 
stakeholders; ii) Incomplete Federal regulations on management regimes allowed on these private set-aside areas; iii) the inexistence of tools for the public sector to conduct strategic planning and management of these set-aside areas at macroscales; and iv) appropriate incentives mechanisms to influence private land-owners in priority areas to adopt practices that would improve biodiversity conservation and ecosystem services provision. This project, that has both pilot and macro policy level elements, aims to address these barriers by a)providing these missing elements, b)by piloting them on-the-ground in two Key Biodiversity Areas (KBA) (approx. 1 mi hectares) and c)via a sectorial agreement with the forestry sector to improve the management of their private set-aside areas. A successful implementation will have a direct contribution of conserving over 50 endangered species, scaling-up sustainable landscape management and appropriate systems of sustainable forest management in millions of hectares of Private Set-Aside Areas (PSAA). More importantly, it will create the basis of a national management system of conservation and management for 88 million hectares of PSAA and their wider landscapes.

The Programme had a very small participation of Indigenous People from Brazil and other Portuguese-speaking countries, while these countries presented alarming scenarios of violence and human rights violations against Indigenous People and other Traditional Communities. Considering such context, in 2023 OHCHR launched a pilot programme in Brazil for an Indigenous Fellowship Programme in Portuguese – it was expanded for Quilombola to adequately reflect the national human rights context. projects.description:
UNDRR provided technical assistance under the MCR2030 initiative to the city governments of Rio de Janeiro (RJ) and Barcarena (PA) to advance disability-inclusion into urban risk management. 

In each city, UNDRR held trainings and workshops to implement the "Addendum for the Inclusion of People with Disabilities to the "Disaster Resilience Scorecard for Cities". The tool guides municipalities to understand the specific needs and capabilities of people with disabilities as an integral part of urban risk management systems and design inclusive disaster risk reduction actions into a strategic plan. The tool must be completed in direct consultation with people with disabilities and their organisations.

Workshops in Barcarena were hold in September 2023 and Rio de Janeiro in October 2023. Both cities are finalising their action plan for disability-inclusive disaster risk reduction.

projects.name: UNEP Transboundary cooperation for the conservation, sustainable development and integrated management of the Pantanal - Upper Paraguay River Basin
projects.description:
The project aims to promote water security through strengthening transboundary water governance, sustainable development, balancing multiple-use and promoting integrated management of the Pantanal-Upper Paraguay River Basin for the social and economic well-being of the population and for the conservation of the freshwater ecosystem, its services, its biodiversity and connectivity.
The project is structured into these components:
Strengthening cooperation for integrated river basin management (UNEP): This component focuses on enhancing collaboration to facilitate integrated management of the river basin.
Consolidating and sharing knowledge and developing a common understanding of the Pantanal-Upper Paraguay Basin: This component, led by both UNEP and IDB, aims to consolidate knowledge and establish a shared understanding of the basin.
Towards trinational planning for sustainable management of the basin: IDB and UNEP jointly lead this component, which works towards trinational planning to ensure the sustainable management of the basin.
On-the-ground interventions promoting integrated water resources management and sustainable finance: This component, led by both IDB and UNEP, involves practical interventions to promote integrated water resources management and sustainable finance.
Awareness building, stakeholder involvement: UNEP leads this component, focusing on raising awareness and involving stakeholders in the project's objectives and activities.

projects.name: IFAD - 2000002694 – Piauí inclusive sustainable rural development achieved (Piauí Inclusive and  Sustainable Project PSI)
projects.description:
The Piauí Inclusive and  Sustainable Project is a collaboration between IFAD, IDB and the state of Piauí and seeks to promote sustainable rural development in the Piauí-Canindé basins in the semiarid region of Piauí with a focus on the interconnected problems of water scarcity, environmental degradation, lack of sanitation in rural communities, low agricultural productivity, and vulnerability of production systems to climate change facing small-scale farmers and vulnerable populations. The overall Project objective is to improve income, food security, access to basic services, and adaptation to climate change of the rural population living in the semiarid region of Piauí. The specific objectives are: (i) improve access to water for domestic use and production; (ii) improve the environmental conditions of rural families and their surroundings; and (iii) increase the adoption of agricultural technologies, with emphasis on climate change adaptation and mitigation, and the integration of small-scale producers, especially women, youth and Afro-descendants, into value chains.

PSI will directly benefit 60,000 families (about 210,000 people), of which 50% will be women-led and 20% youth-led, and at least 4,800 families from traditional communities. Some 31,000 families will benefit from group-based investments and TA to improve production and marketing, 28,000 will benefit from access to water and 6,500 from sanitation. In order to be aligned with IFAD portfolio in Brazil and IDB requirements the PSI will target families. The Project area will cover 138 municipalities. Its geographic targeting strategy is based on the state priority for water investments in the watershed of the Piauí and Canindé rivers in Piauí’s semiarid region, and selects areas with high levels of poverty and vulnerability to climate change, food and nutrition insecurity, and a low human development index (HDI). The target population comprises poor family farmers and poor rural populations, with priority to women, youth and traditional communities, from rural communities facing lower HDI, lack of water and sanitation services, greater limitations in agricultural productivity, less access to TA services, and environmental degradation processes.

projects.name: UNDRR - City-to-city cooperation for climate and disaster resilience fostered via the mentorship of the Resilience Hubs of the "Making Cities Resilient 2030" initiative
projects.description:
MCR2030 Resilience Hubs are cities that demonstrate excellence and leadership in areas of disaster risk reduction, resilience and climate change adaptation. Interested cities can apply to the title of MCR2030 Resilience Hub by signing with UNDRR a Joint Work Plan that aims to mentor nearby local governments seeking support in the local level implementation of the Sendai Framework. 

In 2023, Salvador (BA), Porto Alegre (RS), and Barcarena (PA) have successfully applied to the title and joined Campinas (SP) and Recife (PE) as MCR2030 Resilience Hubs in Brazil. In 2024, the five Brazilian Hubs will support at least 3 municipalities in Brazil with a series mentorship actions, including: city-to-city knowledge exchange; capacity building support to other local governments; mentoring for project planning, strengthening of metropolitan governance for DRR. Those activities will be implemented with the normative guidance and technical support of UNDRR.

projects.name: UNDRR - Disaster Displacement Addendum to the Disaster Resilience Scorecard for Cities piloted in Recife (PE)
projects.description:
UNDRR piloted its Disaster Displacement Addendum to the "Disaster Resilience Scorecard for Cities" in Recife (PE) in April 2023 with the support of IOM, under the MCR2030 initiative. The activity included capacity-building training for city officials of Recife on Disaster Resilience, Climate Change, and Displacements. 

The tool aims to incorporate displacement-affected persons and their specific needs as an integral part of urban risk management systems. It guides local governments to assess current capacities for the governance of disaster displacements and to plan comprehensive disaster risk reduction actions. 

UNDRR will release the final version of the tool next year and deploy it in Brazil with the support of IOM.

projects.name: UNEP Generation Restoration: Catalyzing a nature-based transformation in Finance, Jobs, and Cities
projects.description: The project implements a comprehensive set of measures to address key political, technical, and financial challenges, aiming to promote large-scale restoration, particularly in urban areas. It seeks to raise global awareness of the need for public and private finance to support ecosystem restoration and job creation through nature-based solutions. The project also empowers and inspires city stakeholders—such as government, private sector, and CBOs/NGOs—to replicate and scale up ecosystem restoration initiatives worldwide.  This effort aligns with the UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration and the United Nations Environment Assembly resolution on Nature-based Solutions. The project aims to track investments and jobs and work in nature-based solutions (NbS), as well as to encourage business innovation and job creation in NbS; and, to increase engagement of city stakeholders in restoring urban and peri-urban ecosystems.

framework.description: Meio Ambiente e Mudança do Clima para o Desenvolvimento Sustentável

children.name: 3.1.2 Capacidades de gestão e governança fortalecidas para políticas e programas de estímulo à economia popular, solidária, sustentável e resiliente, a produção, consumo e descarte sustentáveis, a bioeconomia, a inovação, a pesquisa e desenvolvimento ambientalmente adequados e à criação de empregos verdes decentes e inclusivos, valorizando os saberes e modos de vida dos povos indígenas, dos povos e comunidades tradicionais e das populações do campo, floresta e águas em geral e considerando os grupos e pessoas em situação de vulnerabilidade.

children.name: 3.1.3 Capacidades de gestão e governança consolidadas para políticas e programas voltados ao planejamento urbano integrado, sustentável, inclusivo e participativo, com vistas a cidades e territórios eficientes e resilientes adaptados à mudança do clima, socialmente inclusivos, proporcionando a ampliação da integração entre as pessoas, combatendo a poluição, diminuindo o uso dos plásticos e promovendo sua reciclagem.

children.name: 3.2 Até 2027, o Brasil terá avançado na implementação de ações de mitigação da mudança do clima e adaptação aos seus efeitos, redução do desmatamento, de riscos de desastres, considerando os grupos e pessoas em situação de vulnerabilidade, inclusive pessoas forçadamente deslocadas, a partir da perspectiva de geração, gênero, raça e etnia, e proteção dos territórios dos povos indígenas, dos povos e comunidades tradicionais e das populações do campo, floresta e águas em geral, com vistas a promover uma economia resiliente e descarbonizada, à luz dos marcos legais e regulatórios nacionais, e com alinhamento aos compromissos internacionalmente vigentes.

children.name: 3.2.2 Capacidade de gestão local fortalecida, com ênfase em prevenção, preparação, mitigação e estabelecimento de respostas rápidas e duradouras para proteção das comunidades e grupos vulneráveis à mudança do clima e desastres ambientais, que respondam às necessidades e às especificidades dos biomas e com ênfase em seus patrimônios naturais, culturais e respeitem o direito à vida, à integridade física e à saúde das populações afetadas.

children.name: 4.1 Em 2027, o Brasil terá fortalecido, no marco do estado democrático de direito, sua governança, legislação, capacidades e articulação institucionais com ampliação da participação popular para elaborar e executar políticas públicas baseadas em evidências, em direitos humanos e igualdade de geração, gênero, raça e etnia, com vistas à prevenção e ao enfrentamento à corrupção, ao crime e às múltiplas formas de violência, e orientadas às especificidades do território e à transparência, com inovação, cooperação nacional e internacional, e ampla participação da sociedade.

children.name: 4.1.3 Capacidades institucionais fortalecidas para políticas públicas e programas para reduzir as múltiplas formas de criminalidade e violência contra públicos mais afetados e em situação de vulnerabilidade, com especial atenção à violência baseada em gênero e à discriminação racial e contra as juventudes, junto com a provisão de serviços de assistência social e acesso à justiça especializados para vítimas, suas famílias e comunidades.

children.name: 4.1.4 Capacidade do setor público e da sociedade civil fortalecida, com vistas a implementar experiências exitosas, nacional e internacionalmente, inclusive por meio da cooperação sul-sul e trilateral, para otimizar os resultados das políticas públicas.

children.name: 4.2 Até 2027, a sociedade brasileira - especialmente grupos e pessoas em situação de vulnerabilidade - terá maior acesso a bens e serviços públicos de qualidade, à inclusão digital e novas tecnologias, maior capacidade de exercer seus direitos e contribuir com o processo de tomada de decisão, livres de violência e discriminação, para redução das desigualdades sociais e promoção da igualdade de geração, gênero, raça e etnia.

framework.description: Relação das Ações Humanitárias e de Desenvolvimento Sustentável

children.name: 5.1 Até 2027, o Brasil terá suas estratégias, políticas públicas e capacidades institucionais fortalecidas e ampliadas, em todos os níveis de governo e em articulação com o setor privado e a sociedade civil, para prevenir, mitigar e responder a crises humanitárias e desastres, com base em evidências, com especial atenção às populações afetadas, às pessoas refugiadas, migrantes e apátridas e demais grupos e pessoas em situação de vulnerabilidade, em sua diversidade, combatendo a xenofobia e a intolerância e promovendo o respeito aos direitos humanos, a igualdade de geração, gênero, raça e etnia e o desenvolvimento sustentável.
children.description: Até 2027, o Brasil terá suas estratégias, políticas públicas e capacidades institucionais fortalecidas e ampliadas, em todos os níveis de governo e em articulação com o setor privado e a sociedade civil, para prevenir, mitigar e responder a crises humanitárias e desastres, com base em evidências, com especial atenção às populações afetadas, às pessoas refugiadas, migrantes e apátridas e demais grupos e pessoas em situação de vulnerabilidade, em sua diversidade, combatendo a xenofobia e a intolerância e promovendo o respeito aos direitos humanos, a igualdade de geração, gênero, raça e etnia e o desenvolvimento sustentável.

children.name: 5.1.1 Capacidades institucionais fortalecidas para implementar e reforçar políticas, marcos normativos e redes de proteção social e de garantia de direitos, em todos os níveis de governo e junto à sociedade civil, para resposta emergencial, proteção e integração socioeconômica de populações atingidas por crises humanitárias e desastres, pessoas refugiadas, migrantes e apátridas, mulheres, crianças, adolescentes e demais grupos e pessoas em situação de vulnerabilidade, e apoio às comunidades de acolhida.
children.description: Capacidades institucionais fortalecidas para implementar e reforçar políticas, marcos normativos e redes de proteção social e de garantia de direitos, em todos os níveis de governo e junto à sociedade civil, para resposta emergencial, proteção e integração socioeconômica de populações atingidas por crises humanitárias e desastres, pessoas refugiadas, migrantes e apátridas, mulheres, crianças, adolescentes e demais grupos e pessoas em situação de vulnerabilidade, e apoio às comunidades de acolhida.

children.name: 5.1.2 Estudos, coleta de dados desagregados, diagnósticos e metodologias desenvolvidos e centros de estudos e observatórios promovidos para a construção e o fortalecimento de políticas de prevenção, mitigação e resposta a crises humanitárias, desastres, crises geradas pela mudança do clima e fluxos de pessoas refugiadas, migrantes e apátridas, com foco na situação de crianças, adolescentes e mulheres e na prevenção de múltiplas formas de violência nesses contextos.

children.name: 5.1.3 Capacidades fortalecidas de grupos e pessoas em situação de vulnerabilidade, a partir da perspectiva de geração, gênero, raça e etnia, para participar efetivamente de diálogos e formação de consensos sobre políticas, planos, leis e orçamentos, em especial sobre ações de prevenção, mitigação, assistência e resposta a crises humanitárias e desastres e fluxos de pessoas refugiadas, migrantes e apátridas, por meio de mecanismos formulados e implementados em todos os níveis de governo.

children.name: 5.1.4 Capacidades fortalecidas dos governos, sociedade civil e organizações humanitárias para o desenvolvimento de políticas públicas e de estratégias de redução de riscos e gestão de desastres, baseadas em evidências e centradas no respeito aos direitos humanos e na igualdade de geração, gênero, raça e etnia.
